questions.question_text: Which list places the archive numbers $4\,306\,800$, $4\,360\,080$ and $4\,308\,600$ in ascending order?

options.why: Listed the numbers in descending order instead of the ascending order requested.
Compared the last three digits first and put $600$ before $800$, ignoring the higher thousands places.
Placed $4\,360\,080$ too early by not comparing the ten-thousands digits.

questions.question_text: Order the town populations $27\,045\,900$, $27\,405\,090$ and $27\,054\,009$ from largest to smallest.

options.why: Listed the populations from smallest to largest rather than largest to smallest.
Compared the final three digits before the higher ten-thousands place for the last two values.
Treated $054$ thousand as greater than $405$ thousand because it ends in a larger digit.
Compared the ones period $700$ with $770$ before checking the higher thousands period.
Treated the same non-zero digits as equal even though the zeros place them in different columns.
Assumed a comparison cannot be made despite both complete whole numbers being given.

questions.solution_text:
The first difference is in the ten-thousands place: $9>0$.
$103\,009\,770$ is smaller.

questions.question_text: Attendances are $8\,760\,200$, $8\,706\,020$, $8\,762\,000$ and $8\,760\,020$. Which ranks second from greatest to least?

options.why: Selected the greatest attendance rather than the second value in descending order.
Reversed the final comparison between $200$ and $020$ in the ones period.
Selected the smallest attendance after reading second as second from the bottom.

questions.question_text: At which place value do $65\,408\,090$ and $65\,480\,090$ first differ?

options.why: Compared the first digit in the thousands period, but both numbers have $4$ in the hundred-thousands place.
Jumped to the $8$ and $0$ in the thousands place after overlooking the earlier difference in the ten-thousands place.
Selected the highest place shown even though both numbers have the same digits in the millions period.

questions.solution_text: Compare from the left. The millions and hundred-thousands digits match; the first difference is $0<8$ in the ten-thousands place.

options.why: Reversed the first two values by comparing their final groups before their thousands groups.
Placed $309\,100\,001$ before $309\,100\,000$ and then moved the lower-thousands value to the end.
Ordered all four values from greatest to least instead of least to greatest.

questions.question_text: A town population $P$ satisfies $44\,506\,700 < P < 44\,507\,060$. Which value could be $P$?

options.why: Chose a number below the lower bound because $070$ was compared only with the final $700$.
Chose a number above the upper bound by overlooking the tens place in the ones period.
Swapped the ten-thousands and thousands digits, producing a value far above the interval.
